_README.purpose: Hook lines for the first slide of every carousel. Edit this file weekly; it is the one part of the system that goes stale fastest.
_README.why_it_is_separate: Hook formats move in weeks. Book ideas do not. Keeping hooks in their own file means chasing a trend is a five-minute edit rather than a code change, and nobody has to touch the generator to try a new angle.
rules_from_research: 5-8 words. Audiences scroll 3-4 posts per second and the first frame has under 50ms to work.
Promise a payoff, do not just open a riddle. 'You remembered the wrong half' is intriguing and gives nobody a reason to swipe; a stated number tells them exactly what they get.

A number alone is not enough - '5 lessons from X' is what every account posts. The number needs a twist that makes it specific: what survives a real week, what no summary mentions, what people get wrong.
Lead with the reader's stake, not the book's title.
Whatever the hook promises, the carousel must deliver. A hook promising five things and delivering one is worse than no hook.
_README.placeholders: {title} and {author} are replaced. A hook with no placeholder is used as-is, which is usually stronger.
_README.how_to_use_a_trend: When a format is working on your feed, add it here as another entry for the right pillar. The generator rotates through whatever is in the list, so a new hook is live on the next run.
